canonical.:question/problem: Express $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6} \right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
canonical.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u+v) = \sin{u}\cos{v} + \cos{u}\sin{v}
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u = x$ and $v = \dfrac{\pi}{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x+\frac{\pi }{6}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x-\frac{\pi }{4}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{2\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x+\frac{2\pi }{3}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{2\pi }{3}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{2\pi }{3}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}u\operatorname{cos}v-\operatorname{cos}u\operatorname{sin}v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}\left(x-\frac{\pi }{6}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}x\operatorname{cos}\frac{\pi }{6}-\operatorname{cos}x\operatorname{sin}\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}x\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}x}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}x-\operatorname{cos}x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}u\operatorname{cos}v+\operatorname{cos}u\operatorname{sin}v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{5\pi }{3},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}\left(x+\frac{5\pi }{3}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}x\operatorname{cos}\left(\frac{5\pi }{3}\right)+\operatorname{cos}x\operatorname{sin}\left(\frac{5\pi }{3}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}x\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}u\operatorname{cos}v-\operatorname{cos}u\operatorname{sin}v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{7\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}\left(x-\frac{7\pi }{4}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}x\operatorname{cos}\left(\frac{7\pi }{4}\right)-\operatorname{cos}x\operatorname{sin}\left(\frac{7\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\operatorname{cos}x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}u\operatorname{cos}v-\operatorname{cos}u\operatorname{sin}v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{3\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}\left(x-\frac{3\pi }{2}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}x\operatorname{cos}\left(\frac{3\pi }{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}x\operatorname{sin}\left(\frac{3\pi }{2}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}x\cdot 0-\operatorname{cos}x\cdot (-1) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}x \\  & =0\,\operatorname{sin}x+1\,\operatorname{cos}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x-\frac{\pi }{2}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (0)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (1) \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{3\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x-\frac{3\pi }{4}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{3\pi }{4}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{3\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{4\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x+\frac{\pi }{6}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{4\pi }{3}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{4\pi }{3}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\sqrt{3}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{7\pi }{6},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x+\frac{7\pi }{6}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{7\pi }{6}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{7\pi }{6}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{-1}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{5\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x-\frac{5\pi }{4}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{5\pi }{4}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{5\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{7\pi }{4},$ we get

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{7\pi }{6},$ we get

$$

$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{5\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x-\frac{5\pi }{3}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{5\pi }{3}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{5\pi }{3}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x+\frac{\pi }{4}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
